sourceArticle.title: Continually improving our agent harness · Cursor
sourceArticle.author: Stefan Heule & Jediah Katz

athenaOutput.directive: Architect a fully autonomous, self-healing, and model-agnostic agent harness within the Creative Liberation Engine, driven by continuous learning and an intrinsic feedback loop for unparalleled performance and reliability.
athenaOutput.rationale: The provided article emphasizes an iterative, data-driven, and highly customized approach to agent harness improvement, culminating in the concept of an 'automated software factory.' Our directive embraces this by aiming for a sovereign, self-optimizing system that continuously learns and adapts. The preferred option, AIOL, encapsulates this holistic vision by integrating all critical components: robust instrumentation, dynamic context, model-specific tuning, and an automated remediation loop, ensuring the Creative Liberation Engine's agent harness remains at the forefront of AI capability and aligns with our constitutional laws of sovereignty and quality.

options.title: Autonomous Creative Liberation Engine Optimization Loop (AIOL)
options.description: Establish a comprehensive, self-governing system that integrates advanced instrumentation (A/B testing, Keep Rate, LLM satisfaction), proactive anomaly detection, and an automated 'software factory' for diagnosing and self-repairing harness degradations. This system will continuously learn from real-world usage and evaluation signals, dynamically adapting context management, tool configurations, and model-specific optimizations to achieve unparalleled agent performance and reliability.
options.tradeoffs: Extremely high complexity, significant investment in data pipelines, ML/LLM engineering, and robust self-correction logic. Requires meticulous design to prevent unintended consequences from autonomous modifications.

options.title: Dynamic & Adaptive Context Management (DACM)
options.description: Focus specifically on the evolution of the context window. This involves developing advanced techniques for agents to dynamically fetch, filter, summarize, and manage their context, moving away from static guardrails towards intelligent, task- and model-aware context provisioning. Includes semantic search, intelligent file chunking, and dynamic prompt engineering.
options.tradeoffs: Requires robust semantic search and retrieval infrastructure. Potential for increased token usage if not highly optimized. Complex to implement agent-driven context decisions reliably.

options.title: Model-Agnostic Customization Framework (MACF)
options.description: Develop a modular and extensible framework within the harness that allows for deep, automated customization based on the specific strengths and quirks of each integrated LLM. This includes dynamically provisioning appropriate tool formats (e.g., patch vs. string replacement), custom prompting strategies, and model-specific guardrail adjustments without human intervention.
options.tradeoffs: Increased complexity in managing model-specific configurations and their interplay. Potential for significant maintenance overhead as new models are integrated or existing ones evolve. Requires robust validation for each model customization.

options.title: Sovereign Performance & Reliability Observability (SPRO)
options.description: Establish a self-hosted, comprehensive observability suite for the Creative Liberation Engine's agent harness. This includes public benchmarks, internal eval suites (like CursorBench), A/B testing capabilities for real-usage analysis, and custom metrics such as 'Keep Rate' and LLM-based user satisfaction scoring. The goal is to provide a complete, sovereign view of harness performance and identify degradations proactively.
options.tradeoffs: Significant data infrastructure and ML/LLM engineering effort for building and maintaining internal benchmarks and evaluation systems. Requires careful design to prevent metric gaming or misinterpretation.

options.title: Automated Error Remediation & 'Context Rot' Prevention (AERP)
options.description: Focus on the 'tracking and repairing degradations' aspect. This involves implementing sophisticated error classification, anomaly detection alerts (per-tool, per-model), and automated mechanisms to prevent 'context rot' by identifying and purging accumulated mistakes. The system would also automate the creation/updating of backlog tickets with investigations and trigger Cloud Agents for fixes.
options.tradeoffs: Requires highly accurate error classification and anomaly detection models to avoid false positives/negatives. Automated remediation carries risks if not thoroughly validated, potentially introducing new bugs.
